research_question: Among adults undergoing liver (hepatic) resection, what is the effect of fibrin-based haemostatic agents versus active non-fibrin haemostatic agents or standard surgical haemostatic techniques on all-cause perioperative mortality? Pool arm-level deaths using a random-effects risk ratio, defined as risk in the fibrin-based arm divided by risk in the non-fibrin comparator arm.
treatment_label: Fibrin-based haemostatic agent (fibrin sealant, fibrin glue, fibrin patch, or fibrin-coated collagen)
control_label: Active non-fibrin haemostatic agent or standard surgical haemostatic technique (e.g., oxidised cellulose, non-fibrin collagen sponge, argon beam coagulation, electrocautery, or standard surgical haemostasis), excluding no haemostatic agent at all
outcome_description: All-cause perioperative mortality, measured as the number of participants who died in hospital or within approximately 30–90 days after liver resection, according to each trial's definition, divided by the number randomised in each arm. Use intention-to-treat denominators; if only treated or safety-population denominators are available, use them and flag this deviation. Record explicitly reported zero deaths as zero events with the relevant arm total, but exclude trials that do not report mortality. Do not use treatment-related mortality alone or late mortality at one year or more. For multi-arm trials, include the fibrin-based arm and one non-fibrin comparison; combine two eligible non-fibrin arms by summing deaths and participants. Assign arms from treatment descriptions rather than table position. Pool no other outcomes.
positive_direction: For the requested RR, RR > 1 means more perioperative deaths with the fibrin-based agent and therefore favors the non-fibrin comparator; RR < 1 means fewer deaths with the fibrin-based agent. If an SMD/Hedges g direction were ever represented, a positive treatment-favoring g would mean lower mortality with the fibrin-based agent after reverse-coding because mortality is harmful.

inclusion_criteria: Original randomised controlled trials enrolling adults undergoing liver or hepatic resection and comparing eligible study arms.

At least one fibrin-based haemostatic arm (fibrin sealant, fibrin glue, fibrin patch, or fibrin-coated collagen) and at least one active non-fibrin haemostatic-agent or standard surgical-haemostasis comparator arm.
Reports all-cause perioperative mortality, including an explicit statement of zero deaths, with arm-level event counts and denominators sufficient to calculate a risk ratio.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical randomised controlled trial, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, theoretical papers, protocols without results, and non-randomised studies.

No eligible treatment-versus-control comparison: no haemostatic agent at all as the comparator, comparison only between two fibrin-based agents, or otherwise no comparison between a fibrin-based treatment and an active non-fibrin haemostatic agent or technique.

No quantitative all-cause perioperative mortality data capable of producing an effect size (arm-level deaths/proportions and denominators, or other convertible statistics such as an odds ratio); this includes mortality not reported, treatment-related deaths only, or mortality reported only at one year or later.
Completely unrelated to fibrin-based haemostasis in adults undergoing liver resection, including non-hepatic surgery and paediatric-only populations.
moderators_to_extract: Type of fibrin-based agent (sealant/glue, patch, or fibrin-coated collagen)
Type of non-fibrin comparator (topical agent, energy device, or standard surgical haemostasis)
Perioperative mortality time window and definition (in-hospital, 30-day, 90-day, or other within-range definition)
Denominator population (randomised/ITT versus treated or safety population)
Extent/type of liver resection and operative approach (open versus minimally invasive)
Trial characteristics, including publication year, centre status, and sample size
effect_size_note: Extract deaths and totals by correctly identified treatment arm. Estimate a random-effects RR as [deaths/total in the fibrin-based arm] divided by [deaths/total in the non-fibrin arm], with 95% confidence intervals. RR > 1 indicates more deaths with fibrin-based treatment. Retain trials with zero deaths in one arm using an appropriate continuity-correction method; trials with zero deaths in both arms are non-informative for a conventional RR and should not influence the pooled RR, but should be reported descriptively and examined with a suitable sensitivity method if supported. Combine multiple eligible non-fibrin control arms by summing events and totals before analysis. Use randomised denominators whenever available and document use of treated/safety denominators. Assess heterogeneity (tau-squared and I-squared), perform sensitivity analyses where feasible, and report selection and exclusions according to PRISMA 2020.
